title: Sentient Launches Sentient OS to Power Local AI Agents via On-Device LLM
summary:
Sentient, a Y Combinator F26 startup, has released a new software platform called Sentient OS that allows artificial intelligence to run natively on a user's local hardware. The system employs a local large language model to analyze a user's digital context in overnight sessions, providing unlimited inference without the need for cloud connectivity.

The software stores the context it acquires in markdown files owned by the user to ensure the data remains on the device. This architecture is intended to support the deployment of always-on proactive AI agents that can operate at a lower cost than traditional cloud-based models.

selectedTweets.text:
I am still very bullish on local LLMs. We have yet to see its biggest unlock.

I am particularly curious to see what's possible with unlimited inference.

One exciting application is using local models to run always-on proactive agents cheaply.

Great to see Sentient OS pushing for this. It uses a local LLM on your computer to read your context overnight, then keeps what it learns as markdown files you own.
